questions.q: Why does MacLeod say helpful feedback can be a bad sign for your art?
a: If friends can explain it easily, it probably is not original
Friends are usually too jealous to judge creative work
Feedback only matters after a work becomes popular
Most people lack the vocabulary to discuss art
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues the more original an idea is, the less useful advice people can give about it.

questions.q: What does the summary say about starting a blog to earn money from every post?
a: You are better off not starting it at all
You should publish more often to build traffic
You need a paid newsletter from day one
You should pitch sponsors before writing anything
questions.why: Lesson 2 warns that money-driven work stops being art, so get a job to cover the bills instead.

questions.q: How does the book suggest artists cover their living costs?
a: Keep a separate job that pays the rent and bills
Take commissions that match their personal style
Crowdfund each new project before starting it
Teach classes while building a portfolio
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a day job detaches art from money and buys the freedom to make something original.

questions.q: Why does MacLeod think the dream of being discovered is flawed?
a: Artists can now publish and find an audience themselves
Agents rarely sign anyone without a formal degree
Discovery only happens to artists in big cities
Audiences prefer work that comes through galleries
questions.why: Lesson 3 points to platforms like Medium, YouTube and Instagram and says forget the middlemen.

questions.q: Where did MacLeod first draw his cartoons?
a: On the backs of business cards
In the margins of office reports
On napkins at a burger joint
On posters outside his studio
questions.why: The overview explains he drew on business cards so he could create art anywhere.
